source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Derivative weights of the clipped Euclidean Itô process. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Take actual completed Euclidean Itô rows with strongly progressive drifts and almost surely continuous drift paths. Evaluate the test derivative on a coordinate basis vector at the time-clipped state, using the fallback when the state is outside K. The weight is strongly progressive, almost surely continuous on the horizon and bounded there by a deterministic constant.

The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures.
The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T].
The drift coordinates are strongly progressive with almost surely continuous paths on [0,T]. The scalar test is continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.

W_i(t)=Df(\widetilde X_{\min(t,T)})[e_i],\qquad |W_i(t)|\le C_i\quad(0\le t\le T).

theorem anonymous_target.{u_1,
    u_2, u_3}
  {Ω : Type u_1} {I : Type u_2} {J : Type u_3} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J]
  [DecidableEq J] {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : NNReal} {B : NNReal → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ J}
  (hB :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B
      filtration μ)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hUsual : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration μ)
  (η :
    I → J → AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T)
  (A : I → NNReal → Ω → ℝ) (hAp : ∀ (i : I), MeasureTheory.IsStronglyProgressive filtration (A i))
  (hAc : ∀ (i : I), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A i t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T)) {K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ I)}
  (hK : IsCompact K) (fallback : ↑K) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ) (hf : ∀ x ∈ K, ContDiffAt ℝ 1 f x) (i : I) :
  have X := fun t ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 fun k =>
      A k t ω +
        ∑ j,
          AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess (η k j) hT ⋯
            hUsual t ω;
  have W := fun t ω =>
    (fderiv ℝ f
        ↑(local_symbol_9116fdf59d8e fallback
            (X (Min.min t T) ω)))
      ((EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ) i);
  (∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ∀ t ≤ T, X t ω ∈ K) →
    MeasureTheory.IsStronglyProgressive filtration W ∧
      (∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => W t ω) (Set.Icc 0 T)) ∧ ∃ C, ∀ t ≤ T, ∀ (ω : Ω), |W t ω| ≤ C

blind_reconstruction.text:
Finite state index I and Brownian index J; eta_ij, A_i, resulting X; compact K with fallback; ambient scalar f; selected state coordinate i; corrected derivative coefficient W.

Omega is measurable with finite measure mu and a filtration F indexed by nonnegative reals. T>0 is fixed. The Euclidean coordinate type J is finite with decidable equality. B:[0,infinity)×Omega→R^J. lambda_T denotes the pullback under NNReal.toReal of Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T]. I finite with decidable equality; i∈I; A_i scalar processes; f:R^I→R; K⊆R^I. The membership retraction r(y)=(y,proof) if y∈K, and r(y)=fallback otherwise.

Assumptions: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. A progressive L² integrand is a real process a(t,omega), strongly progressive for F, for which (omega,t)↦a(t,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). Each A_i is strongly progressive and has continuous paths on [0,T] mu-a.e.; no bounded-variation hypothesis. K is compact, fallback∈K, f is ambient C¹ at each point of K. Range inclusion holds mu-a.e. simultaneously for all t≤T.

Conclusion: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Set X_k(t)=A_k(t)+∑_j I_j(eta_kj)(t) and W(t,omega)=Df(inclusion(r(X(min(t,T),omega))))[e_i]. Then W is strongly progressive for F; mu-a.e. omega, W(·,omega) is continuous on [0,T]; and there exists C∈R such that for every t≤T and every omega, |W(t,omega)|≤C.

Quantifier order: For every setup, A,K,f and selected coordinate i, if mu-a.e. omega every t≤T satisfies X(t,omega)∈K, then W is strongly progressive, has a.e. continuous paths on [0,T], and there exists a real C bounding |W(t,omega)| for all t≤T and every omega.

Scope: The retraction is used even on exceptional sample points and is evaluated after stopping X at T. Progressivity is global on nonnegative time; continuity is a.e. on [0,T]; the bound is pointwise for all omega on that horizon.

Constant dependencies: C is chosen after all data and selected i; it is uniform in t≤T and omega. The statement does not restrict its dependence further.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.CompactStateRepresentative
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoEuclideanRowRegularity
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcessAfterHorizon
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Comp

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoEuclideanGradientWeights

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 EuclideanBrownianCoordinates ItoIntegralProcess
  ItoIntegralProcessAfterHorizon ItoEuclideanRowRegularity

open CompactStateRepresentative

/-- Evaluating the derivative on a coordinate basis vector along the clipped
actual process gives a bounded progressive weight with continuous paths. -/
theorem euclidean_ito_gradient_weight_progressive_bounded
    {Ω I J : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {T : ℝ≥0}
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ J}
    (hB : IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration μ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration μ)
    (η : I → J → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration μ T) (A : I → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ)
    (hAp : ∀ i, IsStronglyProgressive filtration (A i))
    (hAc : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => A i t ω) (Icc 0 T))
    {K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ I)} (hK : IsCompact K) (fallback : K) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ x ∈ K, ContDiffAt ℝ 1 f x) (i : I) :
    let X := fun (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k : I => A k t ω + ∑ j : J,
      itoIntegralProcess (η k j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual t ω)
    let W := fun (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) =>
      fderiv ℝ f (restrictState fallback (X (min t T) ω) : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ i)
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ∀ t ≤ T, X t ω ∈ K) →
      IsStronglyProgressive filtration W ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ContinuousOn (fun t => W t ω) (Icc 0 T)) ∧
      (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t ≤ T, ∀ ω, |W t ω| ≤ C) := by
  intro X W hRange
  let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ i
  let D (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) := fderiv ℝ f x e
  have hD : ContinuousOn D K :=
    (show ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ f) K from fun x hx =>
      ((hf x hx).continuousAt_fderiv (by decide)).continuousWithinAt).clm_apply continuousOn_const
  let M (k : I) (j : J) := itoIntegralProcess (η k j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual
  have hM (k : I) (j : J) : IsStronglyProgressive filtration (M k j) :=
    (itoIntegralProcess_stronglyAdapted (η k j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j)
      hUsual).isStronglyProgressive_of_continuous
        (itoIntegralProcess_continuous (η k j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual)
  have hRow (k : I) : IsStronglyProgressive filtration
      (fun t ω => A k t ω + ∑ j : J, M k j t ω) :=
    (hAp k).add (IsStronglyProgressive.finsetSum (s := Finset.univ) (fun j _ => hM k j))
  have hAmeas (k : I) (t : ℝ≥0) (_ : t ≤ T) : AEStronglyMeasurable (A k t) μ :=
    (((hAp k).stronglyAdapted t).mono (filtration.le t)).aestronglyMeasurable
  obtain ⟨_, hXc⟩ := measurable_continuousOn_euclidean_ito_rows
    hB hT hUsual η A hAmeas hAc
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro t
    let _ : MeasurableSpace Ω := filtration t
    let cut (p : Iic t × Ω) : Iic t × Ω :=
      (⟨min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T, mem_Iic.2
        ((min_le_left (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T).trans (mem_Iic.1 p.1.property))⟩, p.2)
    have hcut : Measurable cut :=
      ((measurable_subtype_coe.comp measurable_fst).min measurable_const).subtype_mk.prodMk
        measurable_snd
    have hMeas : Measurable (fun p : Iic t × Ω => X (min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T) p.2) := by
      apply (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (I → ℝ)).measurable.comp
      apply measurable_pi_lambda
      intro k
      exact ((hRow k t).comp_measurable hcut).measurable
    let Y (p : Iic t × Ω) : K := restrictState fallback (X (min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T) p.2)
    have hY : Measurable Y := (measurable_restrictState hK.isClosed.measurableSet fallback).comp hMeas
    exact (hD.domRestrict.measurable.comp hY).stronglyMeasurable
  · filter_upwards [hXc, hRange] with ω hω hr
    have hComp := hD.comp hω (fun t ht => hr t ht.2)
    refine hComp.congr fun t ht => ?_
    change D (restrictState fallback (X (min t T) ω) : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) = D (X t ω)
    rw [min_eq_left ht.2, coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr t ht.2)]
  · obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hK.bddAbove_image hD.abs
    exact ⟨C, fun t _ ω => hC ⟨restrictState fallback (X (min t T) ω), (restrictState fallback _).property, rfl⟩⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoEuclideanGradientWeights

steps.title: Clip time in the progressive domain
steps.text: Clip time at T, keep the state when it belongs to K and use the selected point otherwise. The state replacement is Borel measurable, and agrees with the original state throughout the horizon almost surely.
steps.lean:
· intro t
    let _ : MeasurableSpace Ω := filtration t
    let cut (p : Iic t × Ω) : Iic t × Ω :=
      (⟨min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T, mem_Iic.2
        ((min_le_left (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T).trans (mem_Iic.1 p.1.property))⟩, p.2)
    have hcut : Measurable cut :=
      ((measurable_subtype_coe.comp measurable_fst).min measurable_const).subtype_mk.prodMk
        measurable_snd
    have hMeas : Measurable (fun p : Iic t × Ω => X (min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T) p.2) := by
      apply (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (I → ℝ)).measurable.comp
      apply measurable_pi_lambda
      intro k
      exact ((hRow k t).comp_measurable hcut).measurable
    let Y (p : Iic t × Ω) : K := restrictState fallback (X (min (p.1 : ℝ≥0) T) p.2)
    have hY : Measurable Y := (measurable_restrictState hK.isClosed.measurableSet fallback).comp hMeas
    exact (hD.domRestrict.measurable.comp hY).stronglyMeasurable

steps.title: Compose with the derivative entry
steps.text: The derivative entry is continuous on K. Its composition is progressive and almost surely continuous on the horizon. Compactness of K bounds the absolute value uniformly over samples and times.
steps.lean:
· filter_upwards [hXc, hRange] with ω hω hr
    have hComp := hD.comp hω (fun t ht => hr t ht.2)
    refine hComp.congr fun t ht => ?_
    change D (restrictState fallback (X (min t T) ω) : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) = D (X t ω)
    rw [min_eq_left ht.2, coe_restrictState_of_mem fallback (hr t ht.2)]
  · obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hK.bddAbove_image hD.abs
    exact ⟨C, fun t _ ω => hC ⟨restrictState fallback (X (min t T) ω), (restrictState fallback _).property, rfl⟩⟩

lesson.lean_statement: The weight uses the Borel state representative at min(t,T). Progressiveness holds for the entire nonnegative time index.
lesson.lean_proof: Compose the progressive coordinate process with the deterministic clipping map and the continuous derivative entry.
